halfLife.notes: Long and variable half-life due to extensive hepatic metabolism and active metabolites. Once- or twice-daily dosing typical; nocte dosing preferred for sedative effect. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

activeMetabolite.name: 7-hydroxychlorpromazine
activeMetabolite.notes: Multiple active metabolites contribute to prolonged and unpredictable pharmacokinetics. Accumulation possible with long-term use. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

cypInteractions.switchingRelevance: Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors raise chlorpromazine levels and worsen EPS/sedation. Carbamazepine (CYP3A4 inducer) reduces levels. Fluvoxamine (CYP1A2 inhibitor) raises levels. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

metabolicRisk.notes: Significant weight gain, glucose dysregulation. Anticholinergic effects add to metabolic burden. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

lai.notes: No long-acting injectable formulation in current clinical use in Malaysia.

reboundPsychosisRisk.notes: Strong anticholinergic and antihistaminergic properties — significant cholinergic and histaminergic rebound on abrupt cessation. Taper gradually. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.

formulationNotes: Tablets, syrup and IM injection available. Photosensitivity is a notable side effect — counsel patients about sun protection. Monitor QTc. PENDING_CLINICAL_REVIEW.
specialConsiderations: Phenothiazine class — highest QTc risk among FGAs; ECG mandatory at baseline and on dose escalation.
Significant anticholinergic burden — dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, cognitive impairment.
Jaundice (cholestatic hepatitis) — rare but serious; monitor LFTs.
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome risk — common to all antipsychotics but particularly with FGAs.
